# Lambda

Manage functions and execute Python/Node locally or managed runtimes in Docker.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `lambda` |
| Signing name | `lambda` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2015-03-31` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Local processes or Docker runtime |
| Selected operations | 50 of 88 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#lambda) for this service's capabilities.

When IAM authorization is enabled, function-scoped SDK actions and AWS_IAM function URLs evaluate the stored resource policy through the gateway. Each alias/version uses its own policy; an unqualified grant does not grant access to a qualified ARN. Cross-account requests name the full function ARN and require both identity and resource Allow. URL calls need lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction (with lambda:FunctionUrlAuthType and lambda:InvokedViaFunctionUrl), and NONE URLs need a public function policy grant. SNS, S3, EventBridge, API Gateway, CloudWatch alarm, CloudWatch Logs and load balancer invocations are decided by the function policy alone for their service principal, using aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount; dead-letter queues, destinations and event source mappings run as the function's execution role and are decided by its trust and identity policies.

## Limitations and future work

- Local execution is not a sandbox and does not enforce memory or emulate CPU architectures; host interpreter version mismatches warn once and run locally.
- Java, Ruby, .NET, provided runtimes and Image packages require lambda.executor: docker; local interpreter executables must be installed.
- Docker hot reload mounts /var/task read-only and fingerprints metadata; local hot reload hashes contents and runs the host directory with normal user permissions.
- Hot reload does not support image packages, live layers, symlinks or special files; published versions retain a live directory reference rather than a code snapshot.
- Provisioned concurrency does not pre-start environments.
- SourceArn/SourceAccount conditions are absent on ordinary API requests; PrincipalOrgID and EventSourceToken conditions are unsupported.
- Execution-role read checks are cached for 30 seconds per mapping, role and source, including denials; role or source changes force a recheck, deletion drops the entry and reset clears all entries; stream checks use wildcard resources, so a role scoped to a stream ARN is denied; a denied mapping stays Enabled.
- No ImageConfig or event sources beyond the three implemented families.
- Asynchronous work in flight is lost on restart.
- Console ZIP uploads and test events are limited to 1 MiB; larger deployment packages can be copied from S3.
- In identity.mode: verify the console shows function and trigger inventory; management, invocation and log reads require signed CLI/SDK requests.
- Console manages $LATEST; versions, aliases, layers and concurrency use the AWS API.
- Reset ends event source mapping pollers and removes warm execution environments; asynchronous invocations already running can still write records back.
- DLQ targets are validated as standard SQS/SNS ARNs; configuration does not check target existence or execution-role permissions; failed DLQ delivery is dropped and recorded, without emitting DeadLetterErrors metrics.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
